patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient’s mother reports that the infant occasionally stops breathing while sleeping, with episodes increasing in frequency. The patient was born prematurely at 32 weeks due to placental insufficiency and required respiratory support immediately post-birth. Prenatal testing indicated the mother was not immune to rubella. The pregnancy was otherwise uncomplicated, with the mother taking only prenatal vitamins. The family history includes a healthy 3-year-old sister and a father with a heart condition.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Episodes of not breathing (apnea) during sleep

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Premature birth at 32 weeks due to placental insufficiency. Stay in the neonatal intensive care unit for respiratory support.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: The patient’s mother took prenatal vitamins. Father has a heart condition. One healthy sibling.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Patient has pale conjunctiva but no other symptoms or complaints provided by the mother.

questions: During these apnea episodes, does he turn blue or have a low oxygen saturation (cyanosis)?
During these apnea episodes, does he have fever or do you notice any choking/gasping or mucus/phlegm coming from the mouth or nose?
During these episodes, does he turn limp or lose responsiveness afterward (or does he require stimulation to breathe)?
Has the infant had any choking episodes during feeds (coughing, gagging, or color change while drinking), suggesting aspiration as a cause of apnea and worsening cough?
Did the infant have any episodes of choking or turning blue around the time of the apnea (including during feeding, suctioning, or sleeping), and if so how long did the episode last?
During these apnea episodes, have you measured his oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter?
Has he had any measured oxygen saturation at any point during sleep or during a breathing episode (with the pulse oximeter), and what was the lowest reading?
Has he had any measured temperature (fever number) and, if so, what was the highest reading?
Has a pulse oximeter reading been taken while he is actively having the apnea or at the time of his worst breathing, and what was the lowest SpO₂?
Has he had a chest X-ray or any other imaging (and what were the results)?
answers: Patient: I don’t know if my oxygen levels drop, but I haven’t noticed turning blue during the episodes. I do feel short of breath, and my chest pain and purulent cough have been getting worse over the past week.

“I’ve had a fever and I’ve definitely been coughing up purulent, thick sputum. I don’t really notice mucus or phlegm coming out of my nose or mouth separately, but during the episodes I do feel like I’m struggling to breathe.”

I haven’t lost responsiveness or turned limp afterward, and I don’t need to be stimulated to breathe. I mainly just feel very short of breath and the chest pain and cough seem to worsen over the past week.

“I haven’t had any choking during eating or drinking—no coughing or gagging with feeds, and I haven’t noticed any color change with eating. It’s mainly the shortness of breath, worsening left chest pain, and coughing up thick purulent sputum over the past week.”

“I don’t have episodes where I choke or turn blue, including during eating, suctioning, or sleeping, and nothing specific happens around the time of those breathing episodes.” “When I feel the worst, it’s mainly struggling to breathe with worsening left chest pain and thick purulent sputum over the week.”
“I haven’t measured my oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter. I only notice worsening shortness of breath, left chest pain, and thick purulent sputum over the past week.”

I haven’t used a pulse oximeter or checked my oxygen saturation during sleep or during the breathing episodes. I just notice my shortness of breath getting worse along with the left chest pain and the thick purulent sputum over the past week. I don’t know the lowest oxygen reading.

“I’ve had a fever, but I haven’t taken my temperature or recorded the highest reading. I’ve just felt hot with malaise along with the worsening left chest pain, shortness of breath, and thick purulent sputum over the past week.”

“I haven’t used a pulse oximeter at all, so I don’t have any oxygen saturation readings during my worst breathing or during any episodes.” “I can only tell you I feel more short of breath, with worsening left chest pain and thick purulent sputum over the past week.”

“I haven’t had any chest X-ray or other imaging yet. I was seen previously for influenza, but no imaging was done, and my symptoms have been worsening this past week with left chest pain, shortness of breath, and thick purulent sputum.”
